topic: Visualizing Complex Equations: Winding Numbers and Domain Coloring

outline.topic: Visualizing Complex Equations: Winding Numbers and Domain Coloring

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of Complex Numbers
sections.content: Briefly review the complex plane (Argand diagram). Explain that a 2D equation f(z) = w is essentially a transformation of the plane. Use a 'Rubber Sheet' metaphor: imagine the input grid being warped and folded by a function.
sections.example: A grid of squares transforming into a swirling vortex pattern when f(z) = z².

sections.title: Numerical Root Finding in 2D
sections.content: Introduce the Newton-Raphson method extended to 2D complex numbers. Instead of scalar lines, we look for points where the magnitude |f(z)| = 0. We visualize the basins of attraction for different roots.
sections.example: A 'Robot Scout' navigating a landscape of mountains (high values) to find the valley (zero/root) using a gradient descent path.

sections.title: Decoding the Winding Number
sections.content: Define the Winding Number as how many times a curve wraps around the origin. Explain that it is a topological 'fingerprint' of how many roots are enclosed within a loop. Connect this to the Argument Principle.
sections.example: A 'Digital Lasso' circling a region; the number of times the rope wraps around a target 'Treasure' (the root) equals the winding number.

sections.title: Domain Coloring: The Visual Language of Functions
sections.content: Explain how to map 2D complex outputs to color space (Hue for argument/angle, Brightness/Saturation for magnitude). This turns abstract algebra into a continuous, navigable terrain.
sections.example: A 'Color-Coded Weather Map' where specific colors signify phases and intensity levels, revealing zeros as 'black holes' where all colors converge.

sections.title: Synthesis: Solving Equations Visually
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts: Use domain coloring to spot potential zeros, then apply numerical solvers, and verify counts using the winding number. Conclude with the power of visual computation.
sections.example: An 'Explorer's HUD' displaying a domain-colored map, using a winding number scanner to count hidden roots, and triggering a numerical solver to pinpoint them exactly.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of Complex Numbers
lecture_lines: Complex numbers form a flexible 2D plane.
Functions transform this plane like rubber sheets.
Squaring inputs creates a swirling vortex.
animations: Draw complex plane with real/imaginary axes using color #FFFFFF.
Plot point z at (2, 1) and label it 'z' in #FFFF00.
Show vector from origin to z in #FF00FF.

storyboard.title: Numerical Root Finding in 2D
lecture_lines: Numerical root finding extends to complex spaces.
We search for points where magnitude vanishes.
Basins of attraction reveal root locations.
animations: Show f(z) = 0 and mark root with 'X' in #FF0000.
Create a small circular path around the root in #00FFFF.
Highlight the root position with a flashing effect.

storyboard.title: Decoding the Winding Number
lecture_lines: Winding numbers count wraps around the origin.
They act as topological root fingerprints.
This connects geometry to the Argument Principle.
animations: Draw a closed curve in #FFFFFF around the root.
Show the function value mapping the curve in #FFFF00.
Count the windings around the origin with a counter in #00FF00.

storyboard.title: Domain Coloring: The Visual Language of Functions
lecture_lines: Color maps phase and magnitude of functions.
Complex outputs turn into navigable terrains.
Zeros appear as black holes in color.
animations: Display a grid colored by argument in #00FFFF.
Transition color saturation based on function magnitude in #FFFFFF.
Highlight zero-magnitude points as black dots in #000000.

storyboard.title: Synthesis: Solving Equations Visually
lecture_lines: Verify root counts via winding numbers.
animations: Overlay domain coloring with winding path in #FF00FF.
Show the function mapping pushing the root to zero.
Emphasize final solution with a bright ring in #FFFFFF.
